description: We are a team of young innovators building a 'Google Maps for Mars'—an intuitive, multi-layered navigation tool that fuses real NASA data to keep future astronauts safe while maximizing scientific discovery on every Marswalk."
summary:
What We Developed?
We developed Crimson NAV, an early-stage web prototype of an extravehicular activity (EVA) route planner designed for future astronauts exploring Martian locations. Currently in its initial phase, the application combines simulated NASA orbital data including MOLA topography, CRISM mineralogy, and RAD radiation levels into a unified dashboard that calculates three distinct paths between landmarks: a safe route, a mineral-prospecting detour, and a high-risk direct line.

How It Addresses the Challenge?
Crimson NAV bridges the gap between broad orbital maps and hyper localized surface navigation. By layering multiple types of scientific and hazard data together, the tool helps astronauts plan safe Mars walks, manage oxygen and suit battery limits, and target high-value geological sites.

Why It Is Important?
On Mars, astronauts face extreme terrain, lethal radiation, and strict life-support constraints without GPS or immediate help from Earth. Crimson NAV demonstrates how combining multi-layer data into an intuitive navigation tool can protect human explorers while maximizing scientific discovery on a different world.
details:
What It Does and How It Works?

Crimson NAV is an early-stage web prototype of an extravehicular activity (EVA) route planner built for astronauts exploring locations on Mars. Users select a starting base camp and a target landmark on an interactive topographic map, and the system uses a grid-based pathfinding engine to evaluate elevation slopes, mineral deposits, and radiation levels. It instantly generates three color-coded routes: a safe route that avoids steep cliffs and sand traps, a mineral prospecting route that detours over valuable ore deposits, and a fastest direct route that highlights emergency terrain hazards. Alongside the map, dynamic panels calculate oxygen, suit battery, and radiation consumption while updating a required survival gear checklist.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Current NASA planetary mapping tools are built primarily for broad global views rather than localized human spacewalks. Crimson NAV bridges that gap by turning complex orbital science data into an actionable surface navigation. Its intended impact is to keep future Mars astronauts safe from dangerous terrain and radiation exposure while maximizing scientific return during time-limited excursions where GPS and real-time Earth support do not exist.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

Core Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.

AI Development Tools: Google AI Studio and LLM-assisted code generation for rapid prototyping.

Creativity and Team Considerations

Rather than offering a single shortest path, Crimson NAV creatively treats navigation as a three-way tactical trade-off between astronaut survival, scientific yield, and speed. Our team carefully considered real-world human factors on Mars including spacesuit mobility limits on steep inclines, loose basaltic sand sinkage risks, and extreme thermal swings affecting battery drain.
